correctness.rationale: For every integer \(n\ge1\) and positive pairwise distinct squared radii, two-branch polynomial division forces each circle equation to divide \(F=xP+yQ\). Coprimality and \(F(0,0)=0\) force \(F\equiv0\) below degree \(2n\), incompatible with hyperbolicity; at degree \(2n\), its quotient is homogeneous linear. The explicit interpolating field has \(F=yH(s)\), exact degree \(2n\), and positive angular speed on every circle. Its scalar radial variational equation gives \(\log\mu_i=-4\pi a_iH'(a_i)\beta_i/[D_i(C+D_i)]\), with each prescribed sign. Packaged verifier passed 1,414 exact/numerical assertions. The all-parameter conclusion rests on proof, not finite tests.

originality.rationale: The novelty claim excludes known Christopher 2001 degree-m existence, and is confined to simultaneous independent hyperbolic signs at exact degree 2n with first-harmonic cofactor necessity and a closed Floquet formula. Fei 2026 only proves restricted equivariant degree 2n+1 and alternating signs. Margalef-Bentabol and Peralta-Salas 2015 prescribe general stabilities with larger degree bounds. Other inspected contemporary sources address different questions. Full Christopher text could not be inspected, a nontrivial residual risk explicitly retained.

value.rationale: The inverse problem seeks the least polynomial degree needed to realize a fixed set of nested oscillatory circles with arbitrarily designated attraction or repulsion. The known equivariant radial construction has degree \(2n+1\) and alternating signs; the theorem attains degree \(2n\) for all \(2^n\) patterns at the same prescribed radii and proves this degree optimal. The first-harmonic cofactor necessity and explicit multipliers describe the geometric mechanism. Other noncircular cycles remain unclassified and are not claimed absent.
